title: Mid-window steward brief and rollout question hub — Oct 2026
body:
Goal:
A compact steward brief for the mid-window release lane. Single-page reference for the on-call steward and release shepherd during the 72hr steady-state window after initial ramp. Includes a condensed checklist, a 7-step rollback decision path, an annotated 7-day mini calendar for followups, and a draft release-notes snippet to drop into the customer digest.

Context: 
- Release: service-runtime v2.14.0 (internal tag: runtime-v2.14.0-20261001)
- Scope: telemetry sampling change, model routing update (fallback policy added), two small config toggles for batching heuristics.
- Audience: Release steward (owner), SRE rotation, serving-runtime oncall, Product PM for canaries.

Quick runbook (one-line cues):
1) Preflight (T minus 48h): confirm smoke suite green, sampling flags set to staging values, canary route pinned to cohort A (5% traffic). Notify #release-orchestra.
2) Ramp (T minus 24h -> T+4h): 5% -> 20% over 4h, watch P50/P95, error rate, model-fallback counts.
3) Mid-window watch (T+4h -> T+72h): run the steward checklist every 6h, sampling histograms snapshot at 12h cadence.
4) Post-window bake (T+72h -> T+168h): revert debug sampling if no regressions; schedule follow-ups.

Steward checklist (to run at handoff and every 6h):
- Telemetry health (live):
  * P50 latency == baseline +/- 5%
  * P95 latency <= baseline + 40ms absolute
  * 5xx rate <= baseline + 0.03% absolute OR <= 2x baseline (whichever is lower)
  * Model fallback events/day: < 10 per 100k requests (flagged if > 30)
- Error taxonomy quick-scan: increase in botched json outputs, tool-calls failures, or tracebacks in serving logs.
- Resource signals: GPU utilization per shard, queue growth for continuous batching (> 10s backlog triggers throttle).
- Cost delta alert: token-cost per minute increase > 12% -> notify cost-alerts with samples.
- User visible surface: top-3 customer errors in support mentions or SLO complaints in last 6h.
- Canary cohort sanity tests: run prompt set of 30 prompts (quick-check) and inspect 5 manual samples for hallucination/regression.
- Confirm fallback policy adhered to (logs show fallback only on intended model-misalignments).

Rollback decision path (7 steps — use the first step that applies):
1) Critical SLO breach (see SLO thresholds) sustained > 10m and automated mitigation fails -> immediate rollback to runtime-v2.13.x.
2) Reproducible customer-facing degradation (support confirmed) within 30m -> rollback and page PM.
3) Persistent P95 regression > baseline + 120ms for 30m -> throttle to previous variant (policy: revert model-routing to stable) then evaluate.
4) Error-type spike (new 5xx signature > 2x baseline) in frontdoor only -> toggle sampling to previous state and observe 15m.
5) Resource exhaustion risk (GPU OOMs or queue growth causing worker churn) -> reduce traffic to Dedicated lanes and rollback patch.
6) Regressions in quality tests (canary prompt set failure rate > 15%) -> pause rollout and run bisect.
7) If none of the above but negative cost-utility (token cost up > 25% with no quality improvement) -> consider a controlled rollback and run Optimize lab.

Annotated 7-day mini calendar (post-release cadence):
- Day 0 (release day): Canary sweep 0h/1h/4h, steward handoff at 8h and 16h. Customer note stub published.
- Day 1: Telemetry deep-dive at 12:00 UTC (15m), SRE runs smoke replay (3k synthetic requests).
- Day 2: Post-release triage meeting 10:00 (if any anomalies). Schedule A/B evals for model routing.
- Day 3: Sampling histogram baseline comparison and flags cleanup.
- Day 4: Prod cost sampling and quick audit. If stable, mark tickets for config cleanup.
- Day 5: Optional rollback window close (decision by steward + PM).
- Day 6: Finalize release notes and push to docs.

Draft release notes snippet (customer-facing, short):
- What changed: Upgraded runtime to v2.14.0 — improved model routing resilience with a safer fallback policy, updated telemetry sampling to better capture tail latency without raising noise, and small batching improvements reducing per-token overhead for short sequences.
- Why it matters: These changes reduce unexpected inference slowdowns during rare model mismatches and tighten latency signal fidelity for ops teams. Expected user impact: none for the majority of requests; potential improvement in tail latency for latency-sensitive routes.
- Known issues: Some customers using custom routing pins (older SDK versions) may need to re-run the routing sync script (link: CONFLUENCE-1234).

Release-note checklist before publish:
- [ ] Confirm changelog entries include PRs and authors.
- [ ] Run the staged-changelog generator and sanity-check link mapping.
- [ ] PM approval on wording.
- [ ] Legal/Privacy if telemetry flag changes involve sampling PII-suspect fields.

Handoff template for steward -> SRE night shift:
- Current release tag and digest: runtime-v2.14.0-20261001 (sha256: <redacted>)
- Current traffic split: stable: 80%, canaryA: 10%, canaryB: 10% (note: canaryB mirrors rollback-route tests)
- Last successful canary checkpoint: 2026-10-03T04:12Z (smoke suite v3.2 passed)
- Outstanding actions: audit sampling flags, remove staging debug logs from 10/04 if stable, follow up with product on SDK pin doc.
- Contact list: oncall-serving: @serving-oncall, release-owner: Asha P., PM: Marcus N.

Open questions and TODOs (steward/owner):
- Is the fallback policy config transparent enough to customers? (PM action)
- Confirm that sampling retains no raw PII when elevated (privacy review).
- Schedule Optimize-run to simulate cost delta across top-5 routes next week.
- Add a small synthetic workload to surface rare OOMs in the next staging run.

Sticky notes (notes-to-self style):
- If we see odd spike in model-fallback counts, check model-serializer and tokenization mismatch — common root cause in past.
- Keep an eye on queue growth for the new batching heuristic; it trades latency for throughput at extremes.

Appendix: quick signal thresholds (ops shorthand):
- Latency baseline values (from runbook v2.12): P50=38ms, P95=142ms, 5xx baseline=0.02%
- SLO breaching definition: user-visible error rate > 0.5% for 10m OR P95 > baseline + 250ms for 10m

End of brief.

Revision log: 
- 2026-10-03 initial sketch (Asha)
- 2026-10-05 added rollback heuristics and handoff template (Marcus)
- 2026-10-07 telemetry thresholds tuned (Ivy)
